title: Adaptive SLO-breach Decision Engine for Canary, A/B and Shadow Traffic
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Summary: Build a decision engine that automatically recommends and executes rollback/evacuation for model rollouts across canary, A/B, and shadow traffic using a multi-signal SLO framework. The engine will synthesize latency (p50/p95/p99), error-rate (5xx/response-level failures), per-request token cost, and throughput signals into a single action score while exposing tunable sensitivity profiles for different deployment classes (hosted, dedicated, private).

Goals:
- Detect SLO breaches reliably under realistic traffic noise and burstiness without excessive false positives.
- Support cohort-aware decisions (by customer tier, region, route) and contextual baselines (time-of-day, synthetic probes).
- Provide a policy DSL for operators: hard abort thresholds, graded evacuation (traffic fraction reduction), and soft alert-only modes.
- Integrate with Rollouts subsystem to do staged rollbacks (step-down, split-traffic, full-evacuate) and record audit events for every automated action.

Approach:
1) Signal ingestion: collect real-time, windowed metrics (15s/1m/5m) for latency percentiles, request error ratio, throughput (rps), and token-cost-per-request from existing tracing/metrics streams.
2) Normalization & cohorting: normalize signals against rolling baselines per-cohort using trimmed-mean and decayed exponential smoothing to avoid transient blips.
3) Scoring model: implement a hybrid statistical alarm that combines change-point detection (CUSUM + robust bootstrap) for immediate severe shifts and a Bayesian posterior delta for gradual drifts. Each signal maps to a sub-score; sub-scores are weighted by a configurable sensitivity profile.
4) Threshold tuning: offline auto-tuner that runs Monte Carlo simulations over historical traffic and synthetic stress tests to recommend initial thresholds and hysteresis. Tunable knobs include minimum evaluation window, confidence level, and rollback granularity.
5) Decision & action: decision engine outputs an action enum {AlertOnly, GradualReduce(x%), PauseNewCanaries, FullEvacuate, Defer}. Actions executed via Rollout API with audit trail and automatic cooldown.
6) Safety nets: require multiple independent signals or high-confidence posterior to auto-evacuate; for high-impact customers require approval gate.

Acceptance criteria:
- In canary simulation suite (1000 synthetic runs) detect >90% of injected regressions with <3% false-positive auto-evacuations.
- End-to-end latency to trigger action under a high-severity incident <90s from signal onset.
- Integrates with Console: action logged, replayable timeline, and reversible via UI.

Rollout plan: feature-flag gated staged enablement in staging->canary (5% traffic)->global with observability dashboards and an opt-out for Dedicated customers.

Trade-offs considered: aggressive sensitivity reduces customer-visible regressions but increases operator noise; more conservative defaults reduce churn but delay mitigations. Our plan: conservative default with an auto-tune job that recommends profiles per-customer-class.

2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Prototype of scoring pipeline completed (kappa branch). Ran basic synthetic canary tests; CUSUM catches large latency jumps but noisy on bursts. Pushed PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout/pull/2134

2026-03-11 Priya Natarajan (review): Suggest adding cohort weight decay and minimum traffic floor to avoid over-reacting to small customers. Also requested metrics for token-cost drift. Action: add simulation for low-traffic cohorts.
2026-03-12 Data Eng notes: Added streaming metric adapters and a tooling job to compute rolling baselines. Dashboard draft: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/rollouts/slo-decision-engine
2026-03-12 QA: Acceptable detection rates for synthetic regressions: 92% true positive, 2.1% false positive in alert-only mode. Need follow-up for gradational rollback sequencing tests.
Next steps: finish auto-tuner, add canary traffic fraction stepper, create RBAC opt-in for Dedicated customers, and schedule privacy/security review if KMS keys or PII-sensitive signals are added.
